package.title: What If You Never Felt Pain and Didn't Know Until 66?
alt_titles: She Smelled Her Burns Before She Felt Them
This Woman Can't Feel Pain. She Found Out at 66.
description: Jo Cameron, from Scotland, didn't discover she couldn't feel pain until she was 66.

After a hip replacement at 65 and hand surgery at 66 she needed nothing stronger than paracetamol. She often smelled burns before noticing them, her cuts healed quickly, and she scored 0 out of 21 on the GAD-7 anxiety scale.

Scientists traced it to a microdeletion in a gene they named FAAH-OUT, together with a low-activity variant of FAAH. Together they raise her levels of anandamide, one of the body's own pain-dampening molecules.
Would you give up pain? Tell me in the comments.
sources: Habib A. M. et al. (2019), British Journal of Anaesthesia: microdeletion in a FAAH pseudogene (FAAH-OUT) in a patient with pain insensitivity. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6676009
Mikaeili H. et al. (2023), Brain: the molecular basis of FAAH-OUT-associated pain insensitivity.
